site-display.purpose: The story page headline only; one phrase may take Contactless Indigo.

site-headline.purpose: Section heads on the story page.

site-title.purpose: Row and block titles: threats, roles, fallbacks.

site-caption.purpose: Demo labels, platform note, footnotes; faint, never body.

site-count.purpose: The lecturer's live list count; tabular figures.

site-readout.purpose: Decoded values, register rows, times, masked IDs, version, printed URL.

shadows.name: portal-card
shadows.purpose: Every portal card, under its hairline border.

shadows.name: portal-pop
shadows.purpose: Menus, skip link, anything floating above the page.

motion.name: app-ease
motion.purpose: Curves.easeOutCubic: default for app state changes.

motion.name: app-tab-switch
motion.purpose: Bottom-nav active pill and 0.96 to 1.0 scale lift.

motion.name: portal-transition
motion.purpose: Tailwind transition-colors default on buttons and links.

motion.name: site-ease
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out: every site entrance and the tap sequence's reveals.

motion.name: site-press
motion.purpose: Press feedback on buttons and text buttons; hover colours only for (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

motion.name: site-color
motion.purpose: Button background, border and colour changes.

motion.name: site-tap-leaders
motion.value: 180ms scaleX with site-ease-move; IN at 860ms, OUT at 1040ms
motion.purpose: The fastest beat: the tap crossing to the reader and on to the register.

motion.name: site-tap-register
motion.value: list translateY(-36px to 0) 240ms; new row fade-in 200ms; oldest row fade-out 160ms; at 1220ms
motion.purpose: The register grows by pushing rows down inside a four-row window.

motion.name: site-tap-trigger
motion.value: once, at 35% in view; Replay fades out 150ms then reruns
motion.purpose: Rewound before first paint (.motion); 3s .motion-done fallback; reduced motion plays opacity fades only.

motion.name: site-disclosure
motion.value: 200ms rotate(45deg); answer fades in 200ms (translateY -4px), closes instantly
motion.purpose: Threat rows: opening is when the visitor reads; nobody waits for a panel to leave.

motion.name: site-ease-move
motion.purpose: Strong ease-in-out for the two transfers (the leaders) in the tap sequence.

motion.name: site-tap-verify
motion.value: 220ms fade + scale(.96 to 1) at 120ms; check 160ms at 380ms
motion.purpose: Beat 1: the fingerprint-verified line, then its indigo check. The deliberate beat.

motion.name: site-tap-mint
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0), 220ms; payload at 540ms, signature at 600ms
motion.purpose: The signed code arrives whole, left to right (not typed).

motion.name: site-tap-beep
motion.purpose: A 2px indigo ring flashes once on the reader photo.

motion.name: site-tap-count
motion.value: 220ms roll of the last digit (6 to 7) at 1240ms; live dot blinks once (200ms)
motion.purpose: The count goes up, not just changes; tabular figures keep the width steady.

motion.name: site-hall
motion.value: per dot 560ms ease-out from scale(.8) and opacity .5, 7ms stagger in reading order (200 dots in about 2s); turns present green in the last third
motion.purpose: The hall: 200 scattered students snapping into the register when the grid is 40% in view; once; reduced motion shows the grid.

motion.name: site-steps
motion.value: 200ms opacity crossfade between step screens; marker colour 200ms; active band is the middle 10% of the window
motion.purpose: How it works on desktop: the sticky phone follows the step being read. Off below 901px; instant with reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: portal-lg
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes fixed; form/directory grid splits 1/3 + 2/3.

breakpoints.name: site-1100
breakpoints.purpose: Above it the hero buttons never wrap.

breakpoints.name: site-1000
breakpoints.purpose: Stage drops to two columns, photo spans the top at 4:3, leaders hide; hero stacks.

breakpoints.name: site-900
breakpoints.purpose: Text/screenshot splits stack; sticky phone releases.

breakpoints.name: site-860
breakpoints.purpose: Header nav hides; header Install button appears.

breakpoints.name: site-640
breakpoints.purpose: Stage one column, full bleed; primary buttons full width; role rows stack.

narrative.overview:
SUAAMS is a precision tool. In the student's hand it is an instrument on a black ground: graphite surfaces, white type, a faint measuring grid behind everything, and one indigo signal, Contactless Indigo, marking the place to act. Anything a machine says (a time range, a course code, a terminal status) is set in monospace, so the student can tell at a glance what the system reports and what the interface just labels. The check-in moment happens in a queue at a lecture-hall door, so everything on the screen must be readable in one glance and every control must respond the moment it is touched.

The system has two worlds that share one set of meanings. The **app** is dark by default, with a light mode that follows the same rules. The **web portal** is where admins, lecturers and HODs keep records at a desk. It uses a light page, white cards and a dark navy sidebar, with a blue accent for emphasis. The two look different on purpose: one is held in a hand at a door, the other is worked at a desk all day. They share the brand blue in the logo, the four attendance status meanings, and the rule that no status is ever shown by colour alone.

The **public site** at suaams.com.ng is not a third world. It is the app's Midnight Instrument opened up to page width: the same #0F0F0F ground and graphite panels, the same Plex pair, the same one indigo signal, and the same faint 28px measuring grid behind the first screen. Dark is the default and light follows the visitor's system setting, as in the app, so the app's own screenshots sit on the page in their native colours. The only thing that leaves the dark world is the A4 install poster, which is printed on paper and so is light.

Components are **tactile and confident**: full-width 56dp buttons, 48dp+ tap targets, visible press feedback, and a small scale lift on the active item. Motion is short (120-280ms, ease-out-cubic) and only confirms a change. It is never decoration.
keyCharacteristics: App: midnight surfaces (#0F0F0F / #1C1C1C), one indigo accent, IBM Plex Sans + Plex Mono.
Portal: mist page, white hairline cards, navy rail, one blue accent, Plus Jakarta Sans + JetBrains Mono.
Status meanings are identical everywhere: present green, late amber, absent red, excused grey. A text label is always shown.
Every text/surface pair is contrast-measured; values are chosen for AA, not by eye.
Flat surfaces separated by hairline borders; depth comes from tone, not shadow.
Site: the app's world at page width. Ruled rows instead of card grids, Plex self-hosted, indigo the one accent, sample data always labelled demo.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Each world has exactly one accent, and it marks where to act or where you are. In the app that is Contactless Indigo, and it always goes on the same few elements so students learn to find it. It never colours a status value. The site is in the app's world, so its one accent is Contactless Indigo too; Brand Blue stays inside the logo.

rules.name: The Green Is Sacred Rule
rules.body: Green means "you're registered." Never spend it on branding, success toasts for unrelated actions, or decoration. A student reads green in well under a second, so that meaning must stay unambiguous. On the site green appears in two places only: the PRESENT label on the register, and the "75% or more" key that explains the app's Records colours. Both carry their words.

rules.name: The Measured, Not Eyeballed Rule
rules.body: Any new text/surface pair is contrast-checked to WCAG AA (4.5:1 body) before it ships. Status text is checked against the tinted fill it actually sits on, not the opaque colour.

rules.name: The 11sp Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the app renders below 11sp. The only exception is the numeric count inside the notification badge, a single glyph inside a pill. Sub-11 text is a bug, not a style.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace is only for data the system emits (times, session and course codes, terminal states). Never use it for labels, buttons or prose. On the site that means the check-in code, the decoded values, times, masked student IDs, the register count, the build version and the printed URL. Where a machine readout is followed by an explanation, the explanation drops back to the sans.

rules.name: The Theme Scale Rule
rules.body: Text styles come from the theme's text scale (`Theme.of(context).textTheme`, the portal's Tailwind scale). Never hand-roll a font size per screen. That is how the app once had 15 sizes.

rules.name: The Own Fonts Rule
rules.body: The app and the site ship their own Plex files. No Google Fonts or other third-party font host on anything a student opens on campus Wi-Fi.

rules.name: The Borders Separate Rule
rules.body: Hairline borders do the separating, not shadows. If a surface needs more distinction, step its tone. Don't deepen its shadow.

dos: **Do** use Contactless Indigo only on the active tab, the check-in action, contactless glyphs and live dots.
**Do** pair every status colour with its text label, from the one shared map on each side.
**Do** read colours from `AppTerminal` / `colorScheme` (app) or the `@theme` tokens (portal). Never retype a hex at a call site.
**Do** keep app tap targets at 48dp or more, and full-width primary buttons at 56dp tall.
**Do** set times, codes and terminal strings in the mono face, and everything else in the sans.
**Do** contrast-check new pairs against the surface they actually sit on, including tinted fills.
**Do** build site pages from the app's tokens and the `styles.css` custom properties; dark by default, light by `prefers-color-scheme`.
**Do** label every piece of sample data as demo, next to it: the tap, the demo code, the lecturer's live list, and every screenshot caption.
**Do** separate site lists with ruled rows (hairline top and bottom), not cards.
**Do** make every site animation finish into the page's static markup, so no script or reduced motion shows the complete state.
**Do** self-host fonts for anything a student opens (Plex WOFF2, `font-display: swap`).
donts: **Don't** use green for anything except "present / success".
**Don't** render app text below 11sp, or hand-roll a `TextStyle` font size outside the theme scale.
**Don't** use the raw status hues (#10B981, #F59E0B, #EF4444) as text. They are fills only.
**Don't** add drop shadows to app surfaces. Step the tone instead.
**Don't** build portal tone classes by string interpolation (`bg-{{ tone }}`). Use `data-tone`.
**Don't** load Google Fonts or any third-party font on the app or the site.
**Don't** add a second accent to the site, or use Brand Blue anywhere but the logo mark.
**Don't** set prose, headings, labels or buttons in Plex Mono on the site; explanations under a readout go back to the sans.
**Don't** add box shadows to the site. Step from Midnight to Sunk to Graphite instead.
**Don't** carry the poster's light sheet onto screen pages; it is the print exception.
